speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for coming in; I see you are experiencing neck and arm pain, paresthesias, and muscle weakness. To help me understand the severity and location of your symptoms, could you tell me exactly where the pain radiates and which specific muscles feel weak?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Cervical Spondylotic Myelopathy with Radiculopathy.

I have noted your history of diabetes, hypertension, and hypercholesterolemia as risk factors for vascular and degenerative issues. Given your chronic burning pain, paresthesias, and progressive hand weakness, we must rule out cervical spinal cord compression. REQUEST TEST: Cervical_Spine_MRI. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI_Sagittal_and_Axial.
